title: Texas's 30th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: This is an open-seat race for Texas's 30th Congressional District, which covers much of Dallas and southern Dallas County. Incumbent Democrat Jasmine Crockett is retiring to run for the U.S. Senate, creating a rare open-seat contest in one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Texas (Cook PVI: D+25). The Democratic nominee is Rev. Frederick Haynes III, the longtime senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church and a civil rights leader endorsed by Crockett, while the Republican nominee is Everett Jackson, a small business owner and community organizer who won a primary runoff. Given the district's strong Democratic voting history, the Democratic nominee is heavily favored in the general election.
polling_note: No district-specific general election polls were found for Texas's 30th Congressional District. Statewide generic-ballot polls show a close contest between Republicans and Democrats, but the 30th district is considered safely Democratic (Cook PVI: D+25).

candidates.name: Frederick Haynes III
candidates.summary: Frederick Douglass Haynes III is the senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church in Dallas, where he has served since 1983 and grown the congregation from fewer than 100 to over 13,000 members. He is a civil rights leader who briefly succeeded Jesse Jackson as CEO of the Rainbow/PUSH Coalition in 2023, and he won the Democratic primary on March 3, 2026, with 72.4% of the vote. Haynes has centered his campaign on health care access, economic equality, voting rights, and abolishing ICE.

career_history.title: Senior Pastor
career_history.description: Led congregation from fewer than 100 to over 13,000 members; established community programs including THRIVE Intern and Leadership Program and invested over $3 million in HBCUs.

career_history.title: President and CEO
career_history.description: Succeeded Rev. Jesse Jackson as leader of the civil rights organization; served for approximately three months.

candidates.name: Everett Jackson
candidates.summary: Everett Jackson is a small business owner and community organizer from DeSoto, Texas, who defeated Sholdon Daniels in the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff to become the Republican nominee. He describes himself as a community leader who understands the struggles of working families and is running on a platform of economic opportunity, protecting families, constitutional values, and national security. Jackson has criticized outgoing Representative Jasmine Crockett for using the district as a platform for national celebrity rather than serving local needs.
